verdicts.reason: A has a deliberate two-column structure with a dominant headline and a clear CTA, but the subcopy is set almost as large as a headline and sits top-right, so it competes with the headline and reads before it. The pills are in reverse order and are jammed against the right edge, and the right column is cramped. In B the SOLSTICE wordmark falls below the headline, which breaks reading order. B's headline is undersized for the canvas, its pills are reshuffled and wildly inconsistent in width (Honey Rosemary is far wider than the others), and the centred stack leaves the bottom corners dead, so it reads as broken.
